summary: Survival potentials are actually computed by backwardDP and proved equal to surviving path mass. The transformed law needs positive survival only at its initial state; zero intermediate potentials are handled by proved zero support rather than excluded by hypothesis.
source: arxive/playingTheNetworkBackward/main.tex:3696–3743 source conditioned-survival clauses i and path-law part of ii

model_correspondence.evidence: survival N K i s is backwardDP(N-i) on the original shifted kernels with terminal payoff one. Terminal identity, recurrence, [0,1] bounds under substochastic kernels and equality to total full ordinary-path mass are proved independently. The desired survival representation is not a field or hypothesis.

The guarded kernel is K*h_next/h_current only at positive current potential, zero otherwise. Under nonnegative potentials it also equals the total Lean quotient. Weighted telescoping multiplies by the initial potential rather than cancelling intermediate denominators; its zero-start case follows from each nonnegative recurrence summand being zero. Initial positivity is imposed only when deriving a normalized quotient.

model_correspondence.verdict: real visited states, not assumed reachability
model_correspondence.evidence: stateAt recursively reads the actual state after i path transitions. Every nonzero conditioned path from a positive initial potential visits only strictly positive-potential states. Consequently every full path through a zero-potential state has zero mass. No Fintype, recurrence or nonnegative-K assumption is hidden in this support-only lemma; nonzero path factors and nonnegative h suffice.

Positive-potential rows sum to one, dead rows to zero. The full path product equals original surviving mass divided by actual initial survival and sums to one. A zero initial survival instead implies every original surviving path has zero mass; no normalized conditioning on that impossible event is claimed. Horizon zero yields one empty path with survival one.

boundary_cases: two-state chain with initial survival 1/2 and reachable dead ordinary state
actual positive transition into a dead state is pruned to zero
explicit negation of global strict positivity
zero-start surviving path mass and transformed row both zero

negative_controls: reachable dead ordinary state violates global h>0 although initial survival>0
zero-potential transformed row sums to zero, not one
zero initial survival gives no surviving original path and cannot support normalized conditioning
independent_exact_experiment.scope: Exact rational independent completed-cemetery enumeration plus dynamic-program survival. Marginal experiments are supplemental and do not claim a Lean marginal theorem in the reviewed leaf.

scope_limits: This leaf proves the finite ordinary-substochastic-kernel survival and path-factorization clauses. It does not by itself prove the wider source theorem’s conditioned marginals, geometric-mean kernel, Bhattacharyya or Hellinger clauses.
The time convention runs from root at time zero to input at horizon N, reversing the source layer labels without changing the finite trajectory product.
The displayed finite-state type is shared across times; genuinely varying layer state types require the usual tagged-state embedding or a separate bridge.
Only positive initial survival is required for normalized conditioning. No normalized law is claimed at zero survival.

reviewed_contracts.scope: Combined actual substochastic finite-kernel survival theorem: computed [0,1] potentials, terminal condition and recurrence, full path-mass identity, stochastic positive-potential rows and zero dead rows, zero-target support, exact normalized conditioned full path law, and explicit pruning of every path that visits a zero-potential state.
